paragraphs: Axon sells public safety agencies a connected set of hardware and software: Axon Body 4 cameras, Axon Fleet 3 cameras, TASER 10 energy weapons and drones, unified on a real-time crime center platform with an open ecosystem of integrated partners. The company describes itself as an operating system for public safety. TASER 10, its current less-lethal weapon, can deploy up to 10 individually targeted probes without reloading when de-escalation fails.

Axon Fusus puts officer location, alerts, dispatch data, ALPR overlays and video feeds on a single live map so command, field and real-time crime center teams work from the same picture. Residents and businesses can opt in through Community Connect to share their camera video, and those cameras then appear on the Fusus map. The Axon AI Era Plan bundles current and future Axon AI products for a fixed annual cost. Among them is Draft One, which generates first-draft report narratives from audio transcripts of digital evidence and details the officer narrates. Axon Assistant, a voice assistant on the Body 4 camera, translates conversations when no human interpreter is available.

Chief Gary Berg of Campbell PD is quoted saying Fusus lets him see live location, alerts and video from body cams, drones and public safety cameras in one platform. Axon says it is on a mission to cut gun-related deaths between police and the public in half by 2033 through technology, training and trust.
